'''David George Gordon''' (April 15, 1950 – August 4, 2026), nicknamed '''"The Bug Chef"''', was an American [[Natural history|naturalist]] and non-fiction writer.

== Early life and career ==
Gordon was born in [[Chicago]], Illinois, on April 15, 1950, the son of Bernard Gordon, a cosmetics factory worker, and Rosalie Sabath, a high school [[English studies|English]] teacher and [[social work]]er. He was the brother of [[Stuart Gordon]], a [[film director]]. He attended the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]], but dropped out. He moved to [[California]], and he majored in [[biology]] at [[Northeastern Illinois University]], graduating in 1980. During his college years, he worked as an [[aquarist]] at the [[Shedd Aquarium]], a [[public aquarium]] in his hometown.<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/21/dining/david-george-gordon-dead.html|title=David George Gordon, Apostle for Bugs on the Dinner Plate, Dies at 76|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=September 21, 2026|first=Michael S.|last=Rosenwald|access-date=September 21, 2026}}</ref>

He began cooking insects in 1997,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2013/12/16/researcher-turned-chef-whips-up-insect-delights-for-eat-a-bug-cookbook/|title=Researcher turned chef whips up insect delights for Eat-a-Bug Cookbook|work=[[New York Daily News]]|date=December 16, 2013|access-date=September 21, 2026}}</ref> and he appeared in the television talk shows ''[[Nightline]]'', ''[[Late Night with Conan O'Brien]]'', ''[[The Late Late Show with James Corden]]'' and ''[[The View]]''.<ref name="a" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/recipes-from-eat-a-bug-cookbook-2013-7|title=The Author Of The 'Eat-A-Bug' Cookbook Explains How To Make Tarantulas Taste Good|work=[[Business Insider]]|date=July 26, 2013|first=Liz|last=O'Connor|access-date=September 21, 2026}}</ref> In 1998, he wrote ''[[The Eat-A-Bug Cookbook]]'', a [[cookbook]] of insect recipes. He also wrote ''Heaven on the Half Shell'', ''The Sasquatch Seeker's Field Manual'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://davidgeorgegordon.com/#i-started-by-writing|title=David George Gordon|work=Gordon|access-date=September 21, 2026}}</ref> and ''The Compleat Cockroach''. ''[[The New York Times]]'' named him "a young [[Albert Einstein|Einstein]] with a bushy beard, tousled hair and round spectacles".<ref name="a" />

== Personal life and death ==
Gordon's first two marriages, to Maureen Cleary and Mari Mullen, both ended in divorce. His third marriage, to Karen Luke Fildes, a painter, lasted from 2009 until his death. She illustrated several of his books.<ref name="a" />

Gordon died in [[Tacoma, Washington]], on August 4, 2026, at the age of 76.<ref name="a" />
